$schema-note: Example catalogue for M5Stack DinMeter (K134 / K134-V11). Every meaningful discovered example has a disposition, including rejected and inaccessible candidates.

global.build_environment: none - no toolchain installed and no hardware available during this pass

framework_versions_referenced.arduino_board_package: M5Stack Arduino Board Manager v2.1.1 (named in every vendor example header)

examples.title: encoder.ino
examples.author: SeanKwok (shaoxiang@m5stack.com), M5Stack
examples.license_evidence: No LICENSE file exists at the pinned commit and GitHub reports no licence for m5stack/M5DinMeter. The README lists MIT only for M5GFX and M5Unified, and 'original' for the bundled PJRC Encoder.
strengths: Shows the enableEncoder=true argument, the single most common omission
Demonstrates read/readAndReset/write and pressedFor(5000)
Adds a 20 ms 8 kHz click per detent - a good UX pattern
pitfalls: begin() defaults enableEncoder=false
x4 decoding: one detent is four counts, and the example does not say so
examples.selection_reason: Best minimal example for the device's defining feature.

examples.title: display.ino
examples.author: SeanKwok (shaoxiang@m5stack.com), M5Stack
examples.license_evidence: No LICENSE file exists at the pinned commit and GitHub reports no licence for m5stack/M5DinMeter. The README lists MIT only for M5GFX and M5Unified, and 'original' for the bundled PJRC Encoder.
strengths: Shortest path to pixels
Shows both DinMeter.Display and a raw LovyanGFX* draw function
pitfalls: Does not show setRotation or setBrightness
Hides the GRAM offset - M5GFX applies it internally, which conceals something you must know if you drop to raw LovyanGFX
examples.selection_reason: Best minimal display example.

examples.title: rtc.ino
examples.author: SeanKwok (shaoxiang@m5stack.com), M5Stack
examples.license_evidence: No LICENSE file exists at the pinned commit and GitHub reports no licence for m5stack/M5DinMeter. The README lists MIT only for M5GFX and M5Unified, and 'original' for the bundled PJRC Encoder.
strengths: The only vendor example exercising two subsystems together (RTC + Wi-Fi)
Handles the esp_sntp.h / sntp.h header split across IDF versions with __has_include
Explicitly recommends keeping the RTC in UTC
Lands the time-set on a second boundary
pitfalls: Hardcoded SSID/password placeholders
Busy-waits on WiFi.status()
examples.selection_reason: Best integrated example; also the de-facto Wi-Fi example.

examples.title: wakeup.ino
examples.author: SeanKwok (shaoxiang@m5stack.com), M5Stack
examples.license_evidence: No LICENSE file exists at the pinned commit and GitHub reports no licence for m5stack/M5DinMeter. The README lists MIT only for M5GFX and M5Unified, and 'original' for the bundled PJRC Encoder.
strengths: Demonstrates the most device-specific behaviour there is: timerSleep() programmes the BM8563 alarm and then RELEASES the GPIO46 latch - a power-off with an alarm, not an ESP32 deep sleep
Comments show all three timerSleep overloads and powerOff()
pitfalls: Does not explain why the board dies if GPIO46 is not held - the failure mode most users hit first
examples.selection_reason: Best example of the board's defining power architecture; a limit-testing example in practice.

examples.title: buzzer.ino
examples.author: SeanKwok (shaoxiang@m5stack.com), M5Stack
examples.license_evidence: No LICENSE file exists at the pinned commit and GitHub reports no licence for m5stack/M5DinMeter. The README lists MIT only for M5GFX and M5Unified, and 'original' for the bundled PJRC Encoder.
strengths: Minimal; shows tone(freq, ms)
pitfalls: Blocking delay(1000) between tones
examples.selection_reason: Superseded for portfolio purposes by OFF-01, which uses the buzzer in context. Retained for completeness.

examples.title: button.ino
examples.author: SeanKwok (shaoxiang@m5stack.com), M5Stack
examples.license_evidence: No LICENSE file exists at the pinned commit and GitHub reports no licence for m5stack/M5DinMeter. The README lists MIT only for M5GFX and M5Unified, and 'original' for the bundled PJRC Encoder.
strengths: Shows wasPressed/wasReleased
pitfalls: Redundant with OFF-01
examples.selection_reason: Subsumed by OFF-01.

examples.title: M5DinMeter-UserDemo (factory firmware)
examples.author: Forairaaaaa / M5Stack
examples.framework: Arduino via PlatformIO, espressif32@6.3.1, board esp32-s3-devkitc-1
examples.license: MIT (LICENSE, (c) 2024 M5Stack) - MIXED-LICENCE ARCHIVE: bundles PJRC Encoder, ESP32Encoder, I2C_BM8563 and Button, each with its own licence file under lib/
examples.license_evidence: LICENSE at repository root; per-library LICENSE / licence.txt under lib/
strengths: The only complete integrated application
Contains ft_disp_lgfx_cfg.hpp - the authoritative raw-LovyanGFX panel config (offset 52/40, invert true, 40 MHz write, backlight PWM 200 Hz on channel 7)
Every dependency pinned, so it should be reproducible
MIT, so it is a legitimate starting point
pitfalls: Uses a generic esp32-s3-devkitc-1 board, not a DinMeter profile
No partition table specified
Untouched since 2024-03-04
Its 200 Hz backlight PWM conflicts with Espressif's 5 kHz
examples.selection_reason: Best integrated application, and the reference for the raw-LovyanGFX path.

examples.title: espressif/esp-board-manager - m5stack_dinmeter board definition
examples.author: Espressif Systems
examples.license: not verified at file level; esp-board-manager is an Espressif project (their projects are typically Apache-2.0)
examples.license_evidence: not checked in this pass - recorded as unverified rather than assumed
strengths: The most accurate technical description of this board that exists anywhere, vendor documentation included
Documents the GRAM gap (column +52, row +40) and why the application must apply it
Documents the two-channel PCNT quadrature pattern and why GPIO40/41 look double-booked
Documents a real ESP32-S3 build break: en_step_notify_* require SOC_PCNT_SUPPORT_STEP_NOTIFY
Resolves the vendor pin table's GPIO3-vs-GPIO42 ambiguity by citing M5Unified source
Explicitly lists what it does NOT model
pitfalls: Its Grove wire-colour note derives from M5Stack's disputed PinMap, so it is a reproduction and not independent corroboration
Does not model the RTC device, the Grove ports, the charger or USB
examples.selection_reason: Best maintained and reproducible ESP-IDF starting point; also, in practice, the best documentation.

examples.title: bmorcelli/Launcher - m5stack-dinmeter board target
examples.author: Bruno Morcelli
examples.immutable_url: branch link only - no release was pinned at capture time; content captured 2026-09-04
features: SD card over both Grove ports
examples.build_status: not-attempted here, but built by the project's own CI (.github/workflows/main.yml includes { env: "m5stack-dinmeter" })
examples.run_status: reported-working - distributed as Launcher-m5stack-dinmeter.bin, MD5 bccbefef5284357a2a7c3c7cc196fd98, mapped in support_files/m5burner_post.py
strengths: Independent corroboration of the display pins, the GRAM offsets (52/40 and 53/40), the battery divider ratio 2.0, and the absence of PSRAM
Demonstrates a software-SPI SD card across BOTH Grove ports (CS=13 SCK=15 MISO=2 MOSI=1) - the only evidenced way to add storage to this board
Publishes a real partition layout (custom_8Mb.csv, SPIFFS threshold 0x2F0000)
Actively maintained; last push the day of capture
pitfalls: The project README contradicts itself: the port is listed once as [x] and once as [ ] (Beta)
Uses generic board = esp32s3 rather than a DinMeter profile
examples.selection_reason: Best independent cross-check of the pin map, and a practical limit-testing example for Grove-pin reuse.

examples.title: no-body-in-particular/m5din-hikoki
examples.author: no-body-in-particular
examples.immutable_url: branch link only; no commit pinned at capture
strengths: Most-starred DinMeter application found anywhere
A real instrument use case: HiKOKI power-tool battery analyser
pitfalls: Not inspected in depth in this pass
examples.selection_reason: Highest-profile community application; catalogued but not read line-by-line.
